stem: In terms of energy consumption, the brain is quite ____: we humans, for example, have brains that account for slightly more than 2 percent of our biomass, but our brains burn up more than 15 percent of our basal metabolic energy.
Although the committee’s pronouncements are (i)____, consultation with the committee is (ii)____ and in some cases is even mandatory.

With respect to environmental issues, most legal scholarship tends to envision politics as the pursuit of already fixed interests, a view that (i)____ the ability of political communities to (ii)____ their values and their interests through the process of democratic deliberation.

Although the book’s vast notes section (i)____ the impressive breadth of Brzezinski’s research, his (ii)____ seems to fill in the gaps in what his absorption in memoirs and interviews enabled him to learn about the events leading up to the launch of Sputnik, leading him to make (iii)____ claims in some of his descriptions.
Nowadays helium is ____ substance, but just a few generations ago it was an astrophysical conundrum: its spectral lines had been seen in the Sun, but it had never been detected in any other way.

Although the establishment of risk exposure limits and other safety regulations is generally presented as ____, risk-related decisions often contain value-based judgments regarding which risks to accept.

According to A. Elizabeth Arnold, fungi growing inside plant tissue are not causing disease and may in fact protect the plant: leaves of wild cacao trees with abundant internal fungi, for example, ____ colonization by disease-causing fungi.
